message.content:
You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer driver-cmds):
- file: driver/main.cpp:71
- category: dead-code
- title: OptRow::dev is never true -- the dev-filter branch in print_run_block is unreachable
- detail: OptRow (main.cpp:67-72) has `bool dev` documented as "hides it unless ANDESIM_DEV is set" (line 66), and print_run_block filters on it (line 118: `if (o.dev && !is_dev_mode()) continue;`). But every row in kRunOpts (lines 74-90) and kProfileOpts (lines 134-145) initializes dev=false, so the filter never skips anything -- and the kProfileOpts print loop (line 153) does not even consult dev. Contrast TargetRow::dev, which IS live (kListTargets' fixtures row, line 61). The field, its initializers, and the line-118 branch are dead.
- claimed safety: With no dev=true row, deleting the field, the 28 trailing `false` initializers, and the line-118 check produces byte-identical help output in both dev and non-dev mode. If the field is instead kept as deliberate future surface, at minimum the kProfileOpts loop should honor it -- but as-is nothing exercises it.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
